newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid extends gain on higher crude value.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid extends gain on higher crude value.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil climbed again Tuesday on higher crude prices tied to heightened political tension amid reports of renewed Iraqi military movements, industry sources said.
The resid market shrugged off today's sharp decline in natural gas prices, brokers and traders said.
The higher physical quotes reflected stronger forward paper values, but cash activity in New York and Gulf Coast remained thin.
"Everyone is waiting to see who blinks first," said Northeast utility trader.
NYMEX October Henry Hub natgas futures ended down 10.7 cents at $1.791 per million British thermal units, and NYMEX October crude futures finished up 39 cents at $24.12 a barrel.

In the New York harbor, one percent sulfur resid grade was quoted at $17.75-$18.00 a barrel, up from Monday's range of $17.50-$17.75. The three-percent grade was pegged at $15.50-$16.00, up from $15.00-$15.25 on Monday.

In a quiet Gulf physical market, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $16.00-$16.25, flat from Monday's range. Three-percent values were quoted at $15.75-$16.00, unchanged from $15.25-$15.75 on Monday.

New York city gate September gas prices were assessed at as low as $2.02 today, versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.84/mmBtu equivalent. On Monday, September New York city gate gas was pegged at $2.07.
